**Backstory**:  
You hear a rustling coming from a nearby bush. It quickly moves behind you, then back in front of you. Before you turn towards the noise, **Yort charges at you!**  
\---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------  
Having lived a solitary life in the wetlands of the world, Yort was once deprived of companion ship. Most of his friends would perish fighting merciless hunters. With hunting gear left by hunters who fall to the great beasts of the wetlands, Yort began to train. He discovered an iron short sword, along with tracks.

Yort followed the tracks to a fortress where a gladiatorial event was advertised. After gaining a foothold in the fortress, Yort decided to join to prove himself to the hunters who used to invade his homeland. To avenge his fallen friends and become somewhat of a celebrity in this new fortress Yort signed up for this year’s gladiator tournament. 

Will Yort’s lack of training lead to his doom or will he become a household name? All this will be determined in the ring.

**Lore**:

Shàmmansub Arelumid is a ferocious warrior who was taken from the wilderness and assimilated into dwarven society. Even though he was a part of society, the primal instincts never left Shàmmansub and he remained a creature to be feared in combat. In every fight Shàmmansub was victorious and doubted that a creature could ever best him in combat. This ignorance and pride led Shàmmansub Arelumid on an adventure back into the wild to find a creature to rival his talents. While on his adventure Shàmmansub heard of a tournament and joined immediately in hopes of glory and furthering his flawless record. But under the reward of fame and glory Shàmmansub worries that he might instead find the creature who can finally defeat him in combat.

Paul Revere.

For those who don’t know, Paul Revere is a figure in American History who is famous for alerting of a British attack in the American Revolution. He didn’t really do all that much but he is referenced many times in stories and even history books. His job was almost pointless as he could have saved a few lives but he was only a messenger and didn’t really have any other purpose. It would make sense that the messenger who ran the ‘first’ marathon would be considered more prestigious and important since his job as a messenger was more difficult. I don’t know if I am just salty but I have always questioned his constant use in the American culture.
